source_caption:
🎬 Mr. Church (2016)

Mr. Church tells the deeply emotional story of an extraordinary friendship that develops between a young girl named Charlotte “Charlie” Brooks and a talented cook named Henry Joseph Church. Set in Los Angeles during the 1970s, the story begins when Mr. Church is hired to prepare meals for Charlie and her mother, Marie, who is battling a terminal illness. Originally expected to remain with the family for only six months, Mr. Church gradually becomes an irreplaceable presence in their lives, offering much more than delicious meals. Through his kindness, wisdom, and quiet dedication, he provides stability, encouragement, and unconditional support during some of their most difficult moments. As Charlie grows from a curious young girl into an independent young woman, her relationship with Mr. Church evolves into a powerful bond built on trust, respect, and shared experiences. Despite his remarkable generosity, Mr. Church remains deeply private about his own life, carrying personal struggles and painful memories that he rarely discusses. Over the years, Charlie begins discovering that the man who has given so much to others also has his own vulnerabilities and complicated past. Through heartbreaking losses, unexpected challenges, meaningful conversations, and moments of genuine warmth, their relationship demonstrates how family can be created through love rather than blood. Featuring a moving performance by Eddie Murphy, Mr. Church explores friendship, compassion, grief, forgiveness, personal growth, and the lasting impact one extraordinary person can have on another’s life.

🎭 Genre: Drama • Family

⭐ IMDb: 7.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 44m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Bruce Beresford

✍️ Writer: Susan McMartin

source_details.synopsis: Mr. Church is a 2016 American drama film directed by Bruce Beresford and written by Susan McMartin. The film stars Eddie Murphy as the title character with Britt Robertson, Xavier Samuel, Lucy Fry, Christian Madsen and Natascha McElhone also starring. The movie is based on the short story "The Cook Who Came to Live with Us" written by McMartin and based on her life. The film centers around a cook who becomes a caretaker and father figure to three generations of women over the years. This was Murphy's first film role in four years.
